crop.notes: Only the second column of 'The Fizzle' (from the 'Bailed' section to the end). The headline and the whole first column (the excursion on the Continental and the arrests) are on the page but not in the clipping.

ocr.notes: Gist and names mostly readable; many character errors.

summary.suggested: The Missouri Republican printed the Madison County writ against Allen, McCoole and others for the Allen-McCoole fight and an affidavit seeking warrants to stop the Allen-Hogan fight, which fizzled. Allen told a reporter, "there's more days in a year than one."

metadata.notes: Running head reads 'The Missouri Republican, St. Louis, Wednesday, October 29, 1873', page 5. Not yet the St. Louis Republic.

facts.fact: Madison County, Illinois, issued a writ to bring Allen, Mike McCoole, Arthur Chambers, John Looney and others before the circuit court at Edwardsville on an indictment for prize-fighting in the Allen-McCoole fight, returnable November 3
John Renshaw of St. Clair County swore an affidavit asking for warrants against Allen, Ben Hogan and their seconds and backers to prevent their prize fight in Illinois
The Allen-Hogan fight did not come off; police in East St. Louis arrested Looney, Chambers and others from the excursion steamer Continental, and Chambers escaped from the City Hall window
Allen returned to St. Louis that night after the failed fight and expressed his disgust to a reporter near Looney's saloon
Allen on the failed Hogan fight
facts.quote: But never mind, there's more days in a year than one.
